scope: Append-only revalidation of the continental-France early-fourteenth-century aggregate interval. This packet restores the independently supported two-sided interval after a later one-sided floor packet incorrectly superseded it in the active registry.

records.label: Continental France c.1300-1328: revalidated agrarian-demographic upper-limit interval
records.interval_semantics: The 18-20 million pre-Black-Death population interval is divided by the 0.85-1.00 saturation interval, giving an implied capacity interval of approximately 18.0-23.53 million. The population and saturation endpoints are intentionally retained as intervals rather than converted into a point target.
pressure_evidence: Goldstone, Demography, Oxford Handbook of the Ancien Regime, pp. 202-205, identifies 18-20 million within modern French borders at the early-fourteenth-century peak and describes a long-run upper population limit that remained broadly unchanged for centuries.
Pounds, Overpopulation in France and the Low Countries in the Later Middle Ages, Journal of Social History 3 (1970), pp. 225-247, independently documents late-medieval land and subsistence pressure.
Jordan, The Great Famine, pp. 8-12, documents the precarious late-thirteenth/early-fourteenth-century subsistence equilibrium and the 1315-1322 famine shock.
Lot, L'etat des paroisses et des feux de 1328, Bibliotheque de l'Ecole des chartes 90 (1929), pp. 104-107, supplies the 1328 hearth and 528,400 km2 continental envelope used for boundary calibration.

McNeill, Frontier Foods for Late Medieval Consumers, Environment and History 4 (1998), supports predominantly local or regional staple sourcing at this aggregate scale; the 0.85-1.00 local-food interval preserves cross-border and urban-redistribution uncertainty.
shock_flags: The 1328 fiscal observation follows the 1315-1322 Great Famine, so saturation is not forced to exactly one.
Hearth-to-person conversion and extrapolation outside directly assessed royal lands remain uncertain.
Northern France has stronger famine-pressure evidence than southern regions.
The Hundred Years War and Black Death occur after the observation interval.
records.food_regime: rainfed wheat, rye, oats, legumes, livestock, wine, woodland foods, riverine fish, and coastal fish
records.boundary_description: Continental-France envelope represented by modern French borders and Lot's 528,400 km2 departmental reconstruction; mapped to the complete EU5 france_region selector.
records.source_family_independence: The demographic, fiscal, overpopulation, famine, and food-sourcing components are independent source families within one aggregate France evidence bundle; no EU5 population, HYDE, RGO, or model-output field is used.
citation_details: Goldstone 2012, pp. 202-205, especially p. 203 under Histoire immobile?
records.notes: This is an append-only registry repair. It supersedes both the original interval and the later one-sided floor so the same evidence cannot enter twice. It does not add an independent source family; its purpose is to restore the correct two-sided semantics and make the active supersession chain auditable.
